title: LLMs Enable Bag-of-Texts Representations for Short-Text Clustering
problem: LLM similarity judgements used to refine dense embeddings remain tied to the original embedding geometry; existing methods need fine-tuning, known K or proprietary LLMs.
architecture: LeBoT: an embedder retrieves candidate texts for each target; an LLM selects candidates with the same intent; selections are encoded as a bag-of-texts vector over d representative texts (texts initialised equidistant), then clustered with k-means; no embedding optimisation.
llm_or_encoder: gemma-2-9b-it (main); embedders TF-IDF, bert-base, all-MiniLM-L6-v2, e5-large
key_results: With e5-large, LeBoT averages NMI 70.87 / ACC 59.30 over five benchmarks vs 70.53 / 56.99 for DG-CoE (which fine-tunes).
strengths: Training-free and label-free; does not need K for the representation step.
Works with relatively small open LLMs and different embedders/clustering methods.

limitations.text: Effectiveness depends on the LLM; specialised domains may need in-context examples.
Still uses the embedder to retrieve candidates, so a very weak embedder degrades the vectors.

notes: Evaluated under k-means; scalability analysis for large datasets.
